page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, yielding an 8 GB per core memory-to-vCPU ratio. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by a dedicated Intel processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads per core. The CPU configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8), alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. However, multi-core and memory subsystem performance is constrained. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores are rated as poor and weak, respectively. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with read-only large block and write large block speeds registering in the bottom 10% of benchmarks. Similarly, database operations, Redis SET throughput, and software compilation tasks show poor performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-highmem-2 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring a higher memory-to-vCPU ratio without needing high compute density. However, the tradeoff is limited multi-threaded scaling and low memory throughput. This instance is best suited for lightweight memory-bound applications, basic text processing, single-threaded compression tasks, or small-scale web serving where high CPU throughput and local storage are not required.
